ranking_by: electrical conductivity at room temperature, as a share of copper's
subject: metals
title: The 5 Best Metals for Carrying Electricity, Ranked

scenes.text: Gold coats the connectors in your phone. It isn't even the best conductor.
Number five: calcium. As a pure metal, it carries current half as well as copper, and fizzes in water.
scenes.label: Calcium · 50% of copper

scenes.text: Number four: aluminum. Sixty-three percent of copper, but much lighter, so it hangs in power lines.
scenes.label: Aluminum · 63% of copper

scenes.text: Number three: gold. Sixty-nine percent of copper. It's in your phone because it never tarnishes.
scenes.label: Gold · 69% of copper

scenes.text: Number two: copper, the standard every other metal is measured against.
scenes.label: Copper · 100%

scenes.text: Number one: silver. Just six percent better than copper. So why aren't wires silver? It costs far more, and it tarnishes.
scenes.label: Silver · 106% of copper

description:
Electrical resistivity at 20 °C: silver 1.59, copper 1.68, gold 2.44, aluminum 2.65 and calcium about 3.4 (in 10^-8 ohm metres). Compared with copper, that makes silver about 106%, gold 69%, aluminum 63% and calcium 50%.
Copper wins in wiring because it is almost as good as silver at a tiny fraction of the price.
Which metal surprised you most on this list?
first_comment: Would you put silver wiring in your house if it were cheap? And what should we rank next?
